newsitem.title: CROATIA: Opposition journalists back on trial in Croatia.
newsitem.headline: Opposition journalists back on trial in Croatia.

text.p: The trial of two independent journalists charged with defamation of Croatian President Franjo Tudjman resumed on Wednesday after a two-month break.
Viktor Ivancic and Marinko Culic, editor and lead writer respectively of Feral Tribune, a satirical and investigative weekly, were indicted under a new clause in the criminal code.
A verdict in the trial is expected on Thursday.
The defendants face up to three years in jail if convicted.
Diplomats and domestic analysts saw the case as part of the nationalist president's hostility to freedom of the press which has set back Croatia's bid for links with the European Union.

In May, the Council of Europe put Croatia's membership application on hold partly because of problems regarding press freedom. The Council promotes democracy and human rights in Europe, especially in the formerly communist east.
"This trial is not about freedom of press but responsibility for acts against the president of the republic," state prosecutor Visnja Loncar told the court on Wednesday.
"The defendants are trying to politicise the trial, but this is a case of abuse of freedom of the press...freedom of the press cannot be understood as freedom of offence."

Defence witnesses, including Feral's deputy editor-in- chief Boris Dezulovic, asked to identify authors of offending articles and photo montages, said this was impossible because they were joint efforts.
The articles criticised Tudjman's proposal that the remains of members of Croatia's World War Two Nazi puppet regime be reburied at an existing monument for its Serb and Jewish victims.
Tudjman took offence at the way the articles likened him to the late Spanish dictator Francisco Franco.
The human rights group Helsinki Watch appealed to Tudjman on Tuesday to cancel the trial.
"Since your approval is necessary to start the court proceedings, it is clear that, like it or not, this is a political trial," the group wrote in a letter.

Feral Tribune, with its muckraking articles and irreverent photo montages, has long been a thorn in the side of the nationalist government that led Croatia to independence from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.
Ivancic was temporarily detained in 1993 for allegedly dodging military service.
In 1994 the government imposed a huge "pornography tax" on Feral Tribune that could have bankrupted the weekly, but Ivancic had the levy rescinded by court action.
